findings.title: AC-4 live evidence for S6–S8 (and S5, GF1–GF4) predates the gate rewrite; only S1–S4 and S9 were re-run
findings.body: evidence_binding shows S5/S6/S7/S8.summary.json and GF1–GF4.summary.json are byte-identical between tree 078ee162 (2026-10-17 05:26) and head b123b92a; every later evidence tree (6211bee6, c219706d, 83bc0198) differs from head only in S1–S4 summaries. Summaries embed session ids, durations and costs, so identical content means those scenarios were not re-run. Between 078ee162 and head the verification-relevant diff includes gates.py, ghcmd.py, readonly.py, receipts.py, remotecfg.py, state.py, handlers.py, guard.py, maeng-ship and maeng_hooks.py, i.e. the token-taint G3, the closed read-only allowlist, the corrupt-state fail-closed path and the plain-remote/default-head checks. So S7 (G3 denials), S8 (receipt + lease merge) and S6 (harness inert in an eta checkout) were exercised against the previous implementation. The round-5 reviewer already stated the S7 summary came from the old gate; the response was to relax the s7 assertions (g3_denied matches any 'maeng G3' text) rather than re-run, so the PASS rows for S7 B/C do not show the current gate denying. The declared check 'live staging smoke' at head tree b123b92a and the commit message 'staging S1-S9 at 13e7bed' overstate what ran. AC-4 (S6–S8 pass, GF1–GF3 block) is therefore not established for this head. Fix: re-run S5–S9 and GF1–GF4 at 13e7bed/head, commit the new summaries and results, then re-declare the live-smoke check.

findings.title: check_bash fails open on ParseError: unparseable commands skip every G3/G1 check
findings.body: On ParseError the gate returns Decision() (allow) unless RISKY matches a shipping word. The parser raises on heredocs whose delimiter is not [A-Za-z0-9_] with optional matching quotes, e.g. `cat <<\EOF > ~/Documents/Project/eta_v1/f` or `<<"E-OF"`, and on more than 5 nested substitutions; bash accepts all of these. In a personal session such a command is executed with no redirect, token-taint or directory check, so a write into an eta checkout is allowed. This violates the stated rule that a gate must fail closed when it cannot decide. Fix: deny on ParseError (message: rewrite as a plain command / quote the heredoc delimiter), and widen the heredoc regex to accept `<<\WORD` if you want that idiom.

findings.title: `maeng-review store <file>` turns any local JSON into a pass receipt
findings.body: The store subcommand calls receipts.store_verdict on an arbitrary file with no provenance check, no require_personal, and no link to a reviewer run. An agent that cannot get the reviewer to run (the code itself notes the npm codex install is broken) can write {verdict: pass, subject: {...}} with the subject fields that maeng-review prints in a blocked bundle, store it, and `maeng-ship merge` / the lease push will accept it. That is exactly the convenience shortcut the threat model says gates must stop; the receipt mechanism's only value is that passes come from the isolated reviewer. Fix: restrict store to fail/blocked verdicts (revocations), or accept only verdict files written by `maeng-review run` into $MAENG_HOME/reviews/<hash>.json whose hash matches, or remove the subcommand.

findings.title: Runner allowlist: `env VAR=… <runner>` bypasses UNSAFE_ENV and the `$` check
findings.body: _runner only applies UNSAFE_ENV to leading assignments in the raw tokens; program() then strips an `env` wrapper together with all of its `-opts` and `KEY=VALUE` arguments before the remaining checks. So `env PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--collect-only pytest -q` (hook path) or `maeng-verify exec -- env PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--co python3 -m pytest` is recognised as an unfiltered pytest run, exits 0 without executing tests, and records passing test evidence; `env PATH=… pytest` likewise escapes the `$`/backtick check. The same stripping applies to sudo/nice/nohup/command/exec/time. Fix: in _runner (and cmd_exec) treat any WRAPPER_PREFIX token as not-evidence, or at least run UNSAFE_ENV and the `$` check over env's stripped arguments.

findings.title: `gh api graphql` with a file- or substitution-sourced query is uninspectable yet classified read
findings.body: _classify_api only regex-scans the literal field text for `mutation`. `gh api graphql -F query=@m.graphql` (fields=['@m.graphql']) and `gh api graphql -f query="$(cat m.graphql)"` are classified `read`, so route_mentions never fires, canonical_command is not consulted, readonly_strict rejects them only for taint purposes, and check_gh allows them. A file holding mergePullRequest/createCommitOnBranch therefore runs. --input is already denied for this reason. Fix: deny graphql when any field value starts with `@`, contains `$` or a backtick, or when the query is not given as a literal -f/--raw-field.

findings.title: check_mcp_github is a denylist; `delete_file` commits to a branch without tree verification
findings.body: Only push_files, create_or_update_file, merge_pull_request, update_pull_request_branch and create_pull_request are handled; every other non-read tool is allowed after the eta check. github-mcp-server's delete_file commits a deletion to a branch, which is the same unverified-content route as create_or_update_file, and future content-writing tools would also pass. The design elsewhere is allowlist-by-form. Fix: invert to an allowlist of permitted write tools (issue/PR comments, reviews, labels, create_branch, create_issue, …) and deny everything else by default.

findings.title: G3 taint resolves unexpandable `$VAR` tokens (and `cd $VAR`) as personal
findings.body: world_of_path runs os.path.expandvars with the hook's environment, not the agent's persistent shell, so `E=~/Documents/Project/eta_v1; touch $E/x` or `export E=…` in one call and `cd $E && git commit` in the next leave `$E` literal; _abs makes it cwd/$E/…, _nearest_dir falls back to the (personal) cwd, and the mutating segment is allowed. The gate cannot decide such a token and currently decides 'personal'. Fix: for non-read-only segments, treat any token (and any cd target) that still contains `$` or a backtick after expandvars as undecidable and deny with a 'use a literal path' message; accept the extra denials as the fail-closed cost.

findings.title: Configured git aliases are not resolved: `git <alias>` that expands to push bypasses G1
findings.body: route_mentions and check_git only recognise the literal `push` subcommand (and `-c alias.*` overrides). A user- or repo-level alias such as `pushf = push --force` or a `!sh …` alias is a plain `git <name> origin feat`: not read-only, so it reaches check_git, passes _cwd_gate and returns Decision() with no verification or default-branch check. Since `-c alias.*` is already treated as a shipping mention, persisted aliases are the same route. Fix: for a subcommand outside a known builtin set, run `git config --get alias.<sub>`; if it resolves, substitute and re-check (or deny).

findings.title: `gh pr close --delete-branch -R …` deletes the remote head branch under the 'pr write' form
findings.body: pr close is an allowed write with -R; --delete-branch is not filtered, so the remote feature branch is deleted. Not a ship route, but it is a remote mutation outside the described write set. Consider rejecting --delete-branch (and `gh issue delete`) or listing them explicitly in FORMS.

findings.title: must_haves truth 1 is not yet true at this head (loose work-records skill loads in eta_v1)
findings.body: S5 still fails 'no personal loose skills' (harness-run, work-records loaded from ~/.claude/skills) and 'no personal agents' (codebase-explorer). AC-6 is met by its wording (no maeng-harness, zero maeng hook output, eta_v1 unchanged), and the plan dispositions the leak to MAE-224, but the personal record flow is reachable in the eta world until that retirement lands. Recorded so the integration PR is not read as having achieved the truth.

findings.title: PreToolUse matcher omits MultiEdit although gates handle it
findings.body: gates.evaluate and malformed() accept MultiEdit, but hooks.json's PreToolUse matcher lists only Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|mcp__…; if the host still exposes MultiEdit, its writes bypass G3. Add it to the matcher or drop the dead branch.

findings.title: Default mode counts `unittest discover -s <dir>` as unfiltered though an empty directory exits 0 on Python < 3.12
findings.body: unfiltered() accepts any -s/-t directories; `python3 -m unittest discover -s docs` runs 0 tests and exits 0 on 3.11 and earlier, satisfying the default 'some passing tests' predicate. Python 3.12+ exits 5 in that case. Either require -s to be the repository root or pin to 3.12+ semantics by checking the output for 'Ran 0 tests'.

findings.title: Exclusion list accepted as parent exemptions; executable scripts rest on the provenance claim
findings.body: Accepted: archive/ copies, docs/design/*, staging evidence and the skills documented as verbatim or mechanically split in skill-provenance.md / skill-hygiene.md (passed rev6). This exempts executable files such as frontend-slides/scripts/deploy.sh, vercel-deploy/scripts/deploy.sh, chart-style/setup.sh, screenshot/scripts/*.py, diagram-explainer/scripts/*.py and obsidian-workspace/scripts/*.py except private_filter.py, whose verbatim status this review could not verify. Delegated paths (tests, harness-run, work-records, skill scripts) remain uncovered and need their own pass receipts.

findings.title: Round-5 findings: all seven confirmed resolved in this head
findings.body: 1 MCP create_pull_request now passes must_be_origin=True and denies on plain_remote errors. 2 go test -count must match [1-9]\d* and -run is never unfiltered. 3 `file` is absent from the read-only SPECS/PROGS. 4 parse_requirement marks runner-parseable constituents and requirement_met requires source=runner for them; the three runner checks here are satisfied by maeng-verify exec evidence at tree 83bc0198, whose relevant diff to head is empty. 5 state.load raises StateCorrupt on unreadable or malformed state and the dispatcher denies PreToolUse. 6 _checked_registry/_checked_journal raise RegistryError and check_mcp_notion denies. 7 s7 assertions now match any G3 denial (but see the high finding on stale S7 evidence). AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 and AC-5 are met by runner evidence and S4.models.json at head.
